status: LITERATURE ONLY. No experiment, no model, no code change. Every quote is verified verbatim against a text extracted from the paper's own PDF and archived under results/lit/
web_summary_corrections: the figures "22 MBpf" and "0.98 MBpf" attributed to When2com by a web summariser occur 0 times in its text and were dropped
"quarter" occurs 0 times in When2com; "a quarter of the bandwidth" is Who2com's abstract and is cited there only
section_label_note: section labels are hand-chosen and machine-verified: each must occur verbatim, before its quote, with no other declared label between. Automatic heading detection was tried first and rejected -- on these PDFs it returned "4 Mar" and "3 Abstract" as headings

papers.name: Where2comm
papers.b1_quote: The spatial conﬁdence generator generates a spatial conﬁdence map from the feature map
papers.b1: A confidence map produced by a detection decoder run on the agent's OWN feature map, before anything is received.
papers.b2_quote: The request map of theith agent is R(k) i = 1− C(k) i
papers.b2: Ego-side. The ego derives its own request map and sends it; the collaborator then selects what to return. Round 0 uses the sender's confidence alone, so the request only steers rounds after the first.
papers.b3_quote: the communication volume is log2 ( |M(k) i→j|× D× 32/8 )
papers.b3: Defined, not a fixed figure: log2 of selected cells x channels x 4 bytes. The request map itself is H x W and its cost is not separately accounted in that formula.
papers.implication: The only decision input is the ego's own detection confidence, which is exactly the quantity our forest already receives as cues; the request map adds a collaborator-side selector that our single-collaborator setting does not have.

papers.name: When2com
papers.b1_quote: compresses its local observationsxi into a com- pact query vectorµi and a key vectorκi
papers.b1: A learned low-dimensional query from the agent's own raw observation; no ground truth and nothing received.
papers.b2_quote: We further broad- cast the query to all of other agents
papers.b2: Both: ego broadcasts a query, every other agent holds a key, and the match decides who transmits.
papers.b3_label_note: a table header, not a section heading: this paper's experiment-section headings did not survive PDF extraction, so no section number is claimed
papers.b3: MBytes per frame and links per agent, against 2.5 / 5 for the fully connected baselines. The text also states a one-fourth bandwidth ratio, but that sentence is interrupted by a figure's axis labels in the extraction and so is not quoted here. The query's own size is never costed.
papers.implication: The handshake needs a reply from every candidate before the ego can choose, so its decision information is not available to a vehicle that must decide alone.

papers.name: Who2com
papers.b1_quote: compute a matching score, s ji, between their keys, κi∈ Rk, and the request message
papers.b1: A learned key from each candidate's own observation, scored against the requester's compressed request.
papers.b2_quote: the de- graded agent ﬁrst broadcasts its request message
papers.b2: Both, in three stages: request from ego, scores back from candidates, then ego connects.
papers.b3_quote: comparable to centralized ones using a quarter of the bandwidth
papers.b3: A ratio in the abstract. The paper states its selection sends one feature map where centralized baselines send all; the request and score messages are not costed in bits.
papers.implication: The score that decides comes from the collaborator, not the ego, so the information we are looking for does not exist before the exchange.

papers.name: Select2Col
papers.b1_quote: each node corresponds to an agent and comprises its sparse map along with the semantic
papers.b1: A GNN over per-agent nodes, each holding that agent's sparse feature map and its information latency.
papers.b2_quote: receives semantic information transmitted by its neighboring agents
papers.b2: Collaborator-side, and only after arrival: the sparse maps that form the GNN nodes are the received semantic information.
papers.b3: Not given as bits or a ratio for the decision itself. No estimate is offered either, because the selection happens after reception and therefore has no pre-request signalling cost to estimate; the paper models transmission latency instead.
papers.implication: This is a post-reception filter, not a pre-request decision, so it is a counter-example to the question rather than an answer to it.

papers.name: SmartCooper
papers.b1_quote: dynamically adjust the compression ratio based on the channel state information
papers.b1: Channel state information for the compression ratio; sensing-coverage overlap for the judger.
papers.b2_quote: our judger scores reconstructed image sequences based on the union of sensing coverage
papers.b2: Split: CSI is available before transmission, but the judger scores data that has already been transmitted and reconstructed at the ego.
papers.b3_quote: a substantial reduction in communication costs by 23.10%
papers.b3: A ratio against a no-judger scheme. Since the judger runs after reconstruction, the saving is on subsequent rounds, not on the transmission it judges.
papers.implication: Its channel half matches what our arm already has; its task half needs the data first, which is the same wall our rounds 1 to 4 ran into.

papers.name: CoDS
papers.b1_quote: the spatial compression ratio as the fraction of featu res selected for transmission
papers.b1: A selection mask over the sender's own BEV feature map, plus SNR for modulation and code rate.
papers.b2_quote: the CA V ﬁrst employs a feature extraction network
papers.b2: Collaborator-side, before transmission: the CAV decides what of its own features to send. The ego does not request.
papers.b3_quote: Channel Uses = Qd × q C × γs × Rc × log2 Or
papers.b3: A formula in channel uses, with quantisation bits q, spatial ratio, LDPC rate and modulation order -- the same accounting our payload chain uses.
papers.implication: Closest to our transmission model, but the decision sits at the sender about its own data; it does not tell an ego vehicle what to ask for.

papers.name: SemHARQ
papers.b1_quote: the gradients of the task performance with respect to the features are considered
papers.b1: Feature importance from task-performance gradients at the transmitter; distortion of received features at the receiver.
papers.b2_quote: generate a binary feedback vector p(j+1)
papers.b2: Both, but after a first transmission: the receiver evaluates what arrived and feeds back which features to resend.
papers.b3: No figure for the feedback overhead is given. Estimated: the feedback is one bit per feature in the transmitted block, so B bits per retransmission round.
papers.b3_assumption: Assumes the binary vector p is uncoded, one bit per feature of the block just received, and sent once per round; the paper states the vector exists and its indexing but gives neither its length in bits nor a channel for it.
papers.implication: Its decision information is retrospective -- it needs a first transmission before it can rank anything, so it cannot inform a first request.
